new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Points North is looking for a Senior Program Manager who is excited to support the way a growing, 60-person SaaS company gets its most important work done. This is not a PMO role where you install a methodology and police it. It is a hands-on role at a company that has grown on the strength of good people and good instincts and now needs just enough structure to keep that working as we take on bigger things: major product launches, company-wide initiatives, and a brand-new product experiment that needs an owner.

You will report to the VP of Engineering, but you will serve with the whole company. Product and Engineering, then Sales, Customer Success, Client Support, Implementation, Operations, Managed Services, Finance, Marketing, and People and Culture. You will be evolving program and project governance from close to zero, which means you get to decide what good looks like here, and you get to live with the results.

If you are the kind of person who believes the best process is the one nobody notices because it just works, who has seen heavyweight frameworks slow good teams down and has no interest in importing one, and who is as comfortable owning a product backlog as you are running a cross-functional launch, we want to talk to you.

**What You’ll Be Doing:**

* Enhance lightweight program and project governance for Product and Engineering, and then for the company. Collaboratively structure and then document how work gets proposed, prioritized, tracked, and finished. Build the minimum that gives leaders the visibility and teams the clarity they need, and then defend that minimum against the natural pull toward more.
* Run our largest cross-functional initiatives end to end. Major product launches, operational improvement projects, and company-wide changes that touch every department. Own the plan, the dependencies, the risks, the communication, and the follow-through, so that the people doing the work know what they need to do and can focus on the work.
* Support the adoption of AI tools across the company. Not a mandate from above, but a real program: find where AI tooling makes people measurably more effective, help teams try it, learn what works, and spread it. Use AI yourself as a force multiplier in how you plan, communicate, and analyze.
* Be the Product Owner for an early-stage product experiment. We have one engineer dedicated to an early-stage internal tool that may have wider market opportunities. For at least the next six to twelve months, you will own the product side of that experiment: talk with internal and external stakeholders to vet which problems are worth solving, decide how to solve them and in what order, write clear requirements the engineer can build from, and build the evidence for whether there is a larger market. If it succeeds, we will hire a dedicated product manager to hand off to, and you will continue as our Senior Program Manager.
* Make priorities visible and tradeoffs explicit. Help leadership see what is in flight, what is competing for the same people, and what it costs to say yes to something new. Bring data and a point of view and let the executives make the call with clear information.
* Facilitate the Agile events and rituals that earn their keep. Planning, reviews, retrospectives, and the rhythms that keep teams aligned, tuned to what actually helps the team ship rather than what a framework prescribes.
* Build the operating cadence for the company. Quarterly planning, status reporting that people actually read, decision logs, and the handful of templates that make the next project easier than the last one. Document it well enough that it runs without you in the room.
* Partner with every function. Spend real time with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Operations, Managed Services, Finance, Marketing, and People and Culture. Understand how each team works before suggesting how it could work better.
* Close the loop. When an initiative finishes, find out whether it delivered what it promised based on the metrics and success criteria established at kickoff. Run honest retrospectives and share what you learn to improve how we run the next one.
* Continuously learn and grow, in program management, in product thinking, and in how you help a company get better at getting things done.

**What We Are Looking For:**

* A practical thinker who knows the goal is a company that executes well, not a governance model for its own sake.
* A builder of just-enough process. Someone who has seen both ends of the spectrum, chaos and bureaucracy, and has a practiced instinct for the lightweight middle. You know that a process which is not followed is worse than no process at all.
* A practitioner of real Agile software development. You have worked inside teams that actually ship this way, and you understand the principles well enough to adapt the practices to the team instead of forcing the team to fit the practices.
* Someone with enough product instinct to own a product. You can sit with a customer, hear a problem underneath the request, decide what to build first, and write a requirement an engineer can act on without a meeting to decode it.
* A strong communicator who can brief an executive in two minutes, run a working session with a sales or operations team, and write a status update that people read all the way to the end. You follow up on your commitments and your questions.
* Someone who is enthusiastic about AI as an enabler, eager to experiment with AI-assisted tooling in your own work and to help others do the same, without abdicating judgment.
* A collaborator who earns trust across departments by being useful, not by holding authority. People should want you in the room because things go better when you are there.
* Someone who takes pride in enabling others and finds real satisfaction in a team finishing something big and knowing that your work under them made it easier.

* 10+ years of experience in program m

tango is a leader in the home health management industry and is preparing for significant growth! Our mission is to deliver innovative, home-based, post-acute solutions through proprietary technology and proven processes. **PURPOSE**

  

The Quality Assurance Specialist is accountable for and oversees the following tasks:

  

* Validate claims data against information from claims processing systems to ensure that data is accurate (for both auto adjudicated claims as well as manually processed claims)
* Analyze claims data against applicable policies and regulations to identify potential issues (e.g., member benefits, billing anomalies, payment accuracy, claims processing system issues)

* Calculate dollar amount of financial claims errors/defects
* Develop and deliver fact-based audit determinations in an objective, non-confrontational manner
* Escalate issues identified during the audit cycle or rebuttal process to applicable stakeholders, as appropriate (e.g., Operations Team, Quality Team)
* Ensure compliance with applicable audit and rebuttal timelines (rebuttal timelines/form completion, workflows, turnaround time)
* Achieve production quality goals/metrics (e.g., audits per hour, audit accuracy, first-pass accuracy, rebuttal accuracy)
* Provide supporting documentation for audit findings
* Identify/communicate escalated errors/defects and ensure proper resolution, as needed (e.g., rebuttals, appeals)
* Communicate audit findings to applicable stakeholders (e.g., error descriptions, rebuttal information)
* Identify, communicate, and implement opportunities for improving internal audit/rebuttal processes within the Quality team
* Identify, interpret, and utilize applicable claims and audit policies and procedures
* Demonstrate understanding of how various factors may impact claims accuracy (e.g., system edits, keying vendor discrepancies, system logic)
* Demonstrate knowledge of the healthcare industry (e.g., billing practices, terminology, legal/regulatory requirements, coding standards)

  + the administration of all contractual obligations

  + how the processing of accounts receivable and eligibility requirements impacts claims processing
  + vendor data feeds and discrepancy process
  + administrative and regulatory requirements
  + technical workflow processes

  + Claims billing and delinquency procedures

FoodStream Learn is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Program Manager to oversee the strategic coordination and operational execution of our food education programs in NYC public schools.

### **About FOODSTREAM**

At Foodstream, we are building the intelligence layer of food security, connecting people, data, and technology to move food faster, smarter, and more equitably. As a mission-driven, for-profit social enterprise, we use digital infrastructure to link the entire food recovery ecosystem, from donors and distributors to transportation providers and community organizations. Our work operates across two core verticals: Foodstream Learn, an NYC Department of Education–approved program that delivers food literacy and sustainability education in schools and Foodstream Network, which powers real-time food movement and impact tracking. Together, these platforms create a unified model that combines technology, education, and collaboration to reduce waste, expand access, and strengthen community resilience.

### **Description**

### **FoodStream Learn, Nutrition & Culinary Senior Program Manager**

Location: New York City (Remote with regular onsite visits)

* Type: Part-time/Contractor

Compensation: $30 - $40 per hour, based on experience

**About the Role**

FoodStream Learn is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Program Manager to oversee the strategic coordination and operational execution of our food education programs in NYC public schools. This leadership role involves supervising program staff and educators, managing school partnerships, ensuring program quality and compliance, and supporting program expansion. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator, leader, and systems thinker with a track record in education or nonprofit program management.

**Responsibilities**

* Program Leadership: Oversee all aspects of program implementation, ensuring alignment with FoodStream’s mission and educational standards.
* Team Management: Supervise and support junior coordinators, assistants, and educators; lead onboarding, training, and ongoing team development.
* School Partnerships: Maintain and grow relationships with school leaders, administrators, and DOE liaisons; manage communications and problem-solving.
* Logistics & Scheduling: Manage high-level logistics, oversee program calendars across school sites, and ensure all resources (staff, materials, curriculum, etc.) are in place.
* Curriculum Oversight: Collaborate with curriculum developers and educators to align content with school needs, DOE standards, and inclusive teaching practices.
* Monitoring & Evaluation: Lead data collection, impact reporting, and feedback processes to assess program effectiveness and areas for improvement.
* Compliance & Risk Management: Ensure programs meet health, safety, and quality guidelines; troubleshoot operational issues as needed.
* Strategic Development: Support grant reporting, partner communications, and long-term planning for program growth and sustainability.

**Qualifications**

**Required:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Education, Program Management, Public Health, or related field (Master’s preferred)
* 4+ years of experience in program management, school partnerships, or nonprofit operations
* Experience supervising teams or managing junior staff
* Strong leadership, planning, and conflict resolution skills
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Comfort managing multiple projects and school relationships simultaneously
* Proficiency with Google Suite and project management tools (e.g., Airtable, Trello, Asana)
* Access to own transport, valid NY State driver license and computer in good working order

**Preferred:**

* Experience working with NYC public schools or DOE programming
* Familiarity with food education, nutrition, or sustainability
* Bilingual (Spanish/English)
* Experience designing or overseeing curriculum and educator training

**Hours & Contract Details**

* Part-time contract position with flexible scheduling based on school program needs and team oversight
* Hourly compensation of $30 - $40, based on experience and qualifications
* Opportunity to shape program direction and grow within a mission-driven organization

**How to Apply**

Please submit your application via the job post. Thank you.

**About FoodStream**

FoodStream Network (FSN) is a pioneering organization dedicated to transforming food access, education, and distribution through innovative programs and technology-driven solutions.

* FoodStream Learn (FSL) is a DOE-certified food education program that integrates cooking, gardening, and interactive learning to teach food literacy, sustainability, and healthy habits. It empowers individuals—especially students and communities—with the knowledge and skills needed to make informed food choices, grow their own food, and adopt sustainable practices.
* FoodStream Network (FSN) is a digital platform designed to enhance the efficiency and impact of community organizations working to address food insecurity. We connect nonprofits, food industry stakeholders, and community groups to streamline food distribution, reduce waste, and increase access to nutritious food.

$30 - $40 per hour
